title: How to Calculate Your Average Annual Salary Australia: Hourly to Annual with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to an average annual salary Australia using 38-hour weeks, casual loading, and super paid on top. Includes Fair Work and ABS figures.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, equating to $52,253.44 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate and how does it affect my annual salary?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For example, the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour for casual employees. When converting to an annual salary, multiply the casual hourly rate by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks to get the gross annual figure.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on an annual salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your annual salary at 12% of your ordinary earnings (as of 2026–27). It is not deducted from your salary; your employer adds it separately. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $80,000 salary, your employer would contribute an additional $9,600 into your super fund.

faqs.q: What is the average annual salary in Australia according to the ABS?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported in May 2026 that full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week, equating to an average annual salary Australia of approximately $108,352.40 before tax. For all employees (including part-time), total average weekly earnings were $1,579.20, or about $82,118.40 per year.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: From Hourly to Annual

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or checking your current wage, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. This guide uses the latest Fair Work Ombudsman and Australian Bureau of Statistics data to help you calculate your **average annual salary Australia** – including casual loading and superannuation paid on top.

### The Basic Formula

The standard conversion is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. Most full-time roles are based on a 38-hour week, as set by the National Employment Standards. For example:

- Hourly rate: $30.00
- Weekly pay: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Annual gross: $1,140.00 × 52 = $59,280.00

You can also calculate your fortnightly pay by doubling the weekly figure ($2,280.00 in this case). This is useful for budgeting if you're paid every two weeks.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage at $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026 (). This applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most workers are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. Always check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) on our site.

For casual employees, the minimum wage includes a 25% loading, bringing it to $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements like annual leave or sick leave. When converting a casual hourly rate to annual salary, use the loaded rate in the formula. Never add casual loading on top of a rate that already includes it – our [timesheet](/) has a checkbox to apply the 25% loading automatically.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is a key part of your total remuneration. Under the Super Guarantee, your employer must contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, and this is paid on top of your salary – not deducted from it. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer adds an extra $9,600 to your super account, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

When comparing salary offers, remember that the advertised figure is usually your gross salary before super. The super contribution is additional. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice can affect this.

### Average Annual Salary Australia: What the ABS Says

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings data. In May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. Multiplying by 52 gives an **average annual salary Australia** of approximately $108,352.40 before tax. This figure includes all full-time employees across industries.

For all employees (including part-time and casual), total average weekly earnings were $1,579.20, or about $82,118.40 per year. These averages are useful benchmarks, but your actual pay depends on your award, experience, and location. Use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more industry-specific data.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). The Australian Taxation Office provides full details. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator can help you estimate your net income after tax and Medicare.

### Using Our Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) is designed to make these calculations easy. Enter your base hourly rate, check the casual loading box if applicable, and the tool will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. It also estimates super and tax based on the latest rates. Remember, the annual figure assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### Key Takeaways

- Use hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks for full-time annual salary.
- Casual employees should include the 25% loading in the hourly rate.
- Super is paid on top at 12% of ordinary earnings.
- The ABS average annual salary Australia for full-time workers is around $108,352.
- Always check your award or agreement for correct minimum rates.

For more detailed information, explore our [reference tables](/data) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guides.
